facts: There are an estimated 1.3 million Thoroughbred horses in the United States, making it the second most popular horse breed
The Quarter Horse is the most popular horse breed in the United States with an estimated population of 2.1 million horses - about 42% of the total US population
In 2016, the global Shire horse population was only 1500 individuals.
Horse have 10 muscles in their ears.
Horses have a reaction time of 0.3 seconds compared to 1.6 seconds for humans.
Most horses have 205 bones in their body; Arabian's only have 201 bones.
Horses range of vision is 350 degrees, with 55-65 degrees of binocular vision
The average weight of a horse's heart is 9-10 pounds.
Secretariat's heart weighed 21-22 pounds
The average weight of a horse's brain is 22 ounces
Horses don't have a gall bladder
Horses don't have any bones connecting their front legs to the rest of their body.
The smallest horse ever recorded was Thumbelina, measuring just 4hh (17.5 inches) tall.
The tallest horse ever recorded was Sampson. He was 21.2hh (7 feet 2.5 inches) tall and weighed 3,359 pounds.
Old Billy lived from 1760-1822 (62 years) making him the oldest horse on record
The fastest horse over two-furlongs was Winning Brew, whose top speed was 43.97 mph
The fastest horse ever recorded was a Quarter Horse named A Long Goodbye who reached a top speed of 55 mph
The earliest recorded horse race took place in Greece during the 33rd Olympic Games of 648 BC.
According to the FEI, the record for the highest cleared jump is 8 feet 1.25 inches
The longest recorded jump was 27 feet 6.75 inches.
The most expensive horse sold at auction was a thoroughbred colt who sold for $16 million.
The most expensive horse ever sold was a thoroughbred named Fusaichi Pegasus who sold for $70 million.
Horses are unable to burp or vomit due to their cardiac sphincter muscle.
It takes between 9 and 12 months for a hoof to fully regrow
The first horse was cloned in Italy in 2003
Horses can only breathe through their nose
Most horses are born at night
Horses are pregnant for around 11 months
Horses and other Equines have larger eyes than any other land mammal
Horses can sleep standing up, but they only get REM sleep when laying down.
